description: This bar chart, from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the “effect” — likely a performance metric such as probing accuracy or feature importance — of six different multilingual BERT variants across nine language families or categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis (y-axis) represents “effect,” scaled from 0 to 30 with major gridlines at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis (x-axis) lists the language categories in a fixed, non-sorted order. Each category contains up to six grouped bars, each corresponding to a different model variant as indicated by the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Error bars are shown for each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. In most categories, the models show varying levels of effect, with some models (e.g., XLM-B₂ and mBERT-B₂) often achieving higher values, particularly in IE-Indic and Semitic, where effects exceed 20. In contrast, models perform near zero in Uralic and Isolate categories. The IE-Indic group shows the highest overall effects across models, while Uralic shows the lowest. The chart visually suggests that model performance varies significantly by language family, with some models consistently outperforming others within specific groups.
